sanskrit: gurur mato bhavān asya kṛtsnasya jagataḥ prabhuḥ dharmātmānam atas tubhyam anujānīmahe sutam
english: You are accounted the elder of this whole world, its lord. Therefore to you we give our assent concerning your righteous-souled son.

sanskrit: labhatāṃ vīralokān sa sasahāyo narādhipaḥ dvijāgryaiḥ samanujñātas tridive modatāṃ sukhī
english: Let that ruler of men, together with his companions, attain the worlds of heroes; sanctioned by the foremost of the twice-born, let him rejoice in happiness in the third heaven.

sanskrit: prāpsyate ca bhavān puṇyaṃ dharme ca paramāṃ sthitim veda puṇyaṃ ca kārtsnyena samyag bharatasattama
english: And you, O best of the Bharatas, will obtain merit and a supreme standing in righteousness; you know fully and rightly what is meritorious.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭāpadānāś cāsmābhiḥ pāṇḍavāḥ puruṣarṣabhāḥ samarthās tridivasyāpi pālane kiṃ punaḥ kṣiteḥ
english: We have seen the exploits of the Pāṇḍavas, those bulls among men; they are capable of governing even heaven, how much more the earth.

sanskrit: anuvatsyanti cāpīmāḥ sameṣu viṣameṣu ca prajāḥ kurukulaśreṣṭha pāṇḍavāñ śīlabhūṣaṇān
english: And these subjects will follow the Pāṇḍavas, adorned with good character, O best of the Kuru line, in fair times and foul alike.

sanskrit: brahmadeyāgrahārāṃś ca parihārāṃś ca pārthiva pūrvarājātisargāṃś ca pālayaty eva pāṇḍavaḥ
english: The grants of land bestowed upon brahmins, the exemptions, O king, and the endowments made by former kings—the Pāṇḍava upholds them all.

sanskrit: dīrghadarśī kṛtaprajñaḥ sadā vaiśravaṇo yathā akṣudrasacivaś cāyaṃ kuntīputro mahāmanāḥ
english: Far-seeing and accomplished in wisdom, ever like Vaiśravaṇa, this high-minded son of Kuntī has no petty counsellors.

sanskrit: apy amitre dayāvāṃś ca śuciś ca bharatarṣabha ṛju paśyati medhāvī putravat pāti naḥ sadā
english: Compassionate even toward a foe, and pure, O bull of the Bharatas, the wise one looks upon things with uprightness and ever protects us as if we were his children.

sanskrit: vipriyaṃ ca janasyāsya saṃsargād dharmajasya vai na kariṣyanti rājarṣe tathā bhīmārjunādayaḥ
english: And through their fellowship with the son of Dharma, O royal sage, neither Bhīma nor Arjuna nor the rest will do anything displeasing to these people.

sanskrit: mandā mṛduṣu kauravyās tīkṣṇeṣv āśīviṣopamāḥ vīryavanto mahātmānaḥ paurāṇāṃ ca hite ratāḥ
english: Gentle toward the gentle are these Kauravyas, but like venomous serpents toward the harsh; valiant, great-souled, and devoted to the welfare of the citizens.

sanskrit: na kuntī na ca pāñcālī na colūpī na sātvatī asmiñ jane kariṣyanti pratikūlāni karhi cit
english: Neither Kuntī, nor the Pāñcāla princess, nor Ulūpī, nor the Sātvatī woman will ever do anything contrary to the good of these people.

sanskrit: bhavatkṛtam imaṃ snehaṃ yudhiṣṭhiravivardhitam na pṛṣṭhataḥ kariṣyanti paurajānapadā janāḥ
english: The affection you have shown, which Yudhiṣṭhira has nurtured, the people of city and countryside will not cast behind their backs.

sanskrit: adharmiṣṭhān api sataḥ kuntīputrā mahārathāḥ mānavān pālayiṣyanti bhūtvā dharmaparāyaṇāḥ
english: Even men given to unrighteousness the sons of Kuntī, those mighty charioteers, will protect, themselves remaining wholly devoted to righteousness.

sanskrit: sa rājan mānasaṃ duḥkham apanīya yudhiṣṭhirāt kuru kāryāṇi dharmyāṇi namas te bharatarṣabha
english: Therefore, O king, putting away from yourself any grief of mind concerning Yudhiṣṭhira, perform your righteous duties; homage to you, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasya tad vacanaṃ dharmyam anubandhaguṇottaram sādhu sādhv iti sarvaḥ sa janaḥ pratigṛhītavān
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: That righteous speech of his, excellent in its bearing upon the matter at hand, all that assembly received with cries of "Well said, well said!"

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭraś ca tad vākyam abhipūjya punaḥ punaḥ visarjayām āsa tadā sarvās tu prakṛtīḥ śanaiḥ
english: And Dhṛtarāṣṭra, honoring that speech again and again, then gently dismissed all his subjects.

sanskrit: sa taiḥ saṃpūjito rājā śivenāvekṣitas tadā prāñjaliḥ pūjayām āsa taṃ janaṃ bharatarṣabha
english: That king, honored by them and regarded with kindly eyes, then with joined palms honored that people in turn, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tato viveśa bhuvanaṃ gāndhāryā sahito nṛpaḥ vyuṣṭāyāṃ caiva śarvaryāṃ yac cakāra nibodha tat
english: Then the king entered his dwelling together with Gāndhārī; and learn now what he did when the night had passed.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca vyuṣitāyāṃ rajanyāṃ tu dhṛtarāṣṭro 'mbikāsutaḥ viduraṃ preṣayām āsa yudhiṣṭhiraniveśanam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When the night had passed, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the son of Ambikā, sent Vidura to the dwelling of Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: sa gatvā rājavacanād uvācācyutam īśvaram yudhiṣṭhiraṃ mahātejāḥ sarvabuddhimatāṃ varaḥ
english: He, the greatly lustrous one, foremost of all the wise, having gone at the king's bidding, addressed the unfailing sovereign Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭro mahārāja vanavāsāya dīkṣitaḥ gamiṣyati vanaṃ rājan kārttikīm āgatām imām
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O great king, has resolved upon dwelling in the forest; he will go to the forest, O king, now that this full-moon of Kārttika has come.

sanskrit: sa tvā kurukulaśreṣṭha kiṃ cid artham abhīpsati śrāddham icchati dātuṃ sa gāṅgeyasya mahātmanaḥ
english: He desires of you a certain thing, O best of the Kuru line; he wishes to offer a śrāddha for the great-souled son of Gaṅgā,

sanskrit: droṇasya somadattasya bāhlīkasya ca dhīmataḥ putrāṇāṃ caiva sarveṣāṃ ye cāsya suhṛdo hatāḥ yadi cābhyanujānīṣe saindhavāpasadasya ca
english: and for Droṇa, for Somadatta, and for the wise Bāhlīka, and for all his sons and for those friends of his who were slain—and, if you grant leave, for that vile Saindhava as well.

sanskrit: etac chrutvā tu vacanaṃ vidurasya yudhiṣṭhiraḥ hṛṣṭaḥ saṃpūjayām āsa guḍākeśaś ca pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Hearing this speech of Vidura, Yudhiṣṭhira was gladdened and paid him honor, as did the Pāṇḍava Guḍākeśa.

sanskrit: na tu bhīmo dṛḍhakrodhas tad vaco jagṛhe tadā vidurasya mahātejā duryodhanakṛtaṃ smaran
english: But Bhīma of firm wrath and great lustre did not then accept that speech of Vidura, remembering what Duryodhana had done.

sanskrit: abhiprāyaṃ viditvā tu bhīmasenasya phalgunaḥ kirīṭī kiṃ cid ānamya bhīmaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: But Phalguna, the diademed one, knowing Bhīmasena's intent, bowing a little, spoke these words to Bhīma:

sanskrit: bhīma rājā pitā vṛddho vanavāsāya dīkṣitaḥ dātum icchati sarveṣāṃ suhṛdām aurdhvadehikam
english: "Bhīma, the aged king our father, resolved upon dwelling in the forest, wishes to make the funeral offerings for all his friends.

sanskrit: bhavatā nirjitaṃ vittaṃ dātum icchati kauravaḥ bhīṣmādīnāṃ mahābāho tad anujñātum arhasi
english: With the wealth won by you, O mighty-armed one, the Kaurava wishes to make gifts on behalf of Bhīṣma and the rest; it is fitting that you grant leave for this."

sanskrit: diṣṭyā tv adya mahābāho dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ prayācati yācito yaḥ purāsmābhiḥ paśya kālasya paryayam
english: "By good fortune, O mighty-armed one, Dhṛtarāṣṭra now entreats us—he whom we once entreated. Behold the turning of time!

sanskrit: yo 'sau pṛthivyāḥ kṛtsnāyā bhartā bhūtvā narādhipaḥ parair vinihatāpatyo vanaṃ gantum abhīpsati
english: He who was lord of the whole earth, a ruler of men, his offspring slain by his foes, now longs to go to the forest.

sanskrit: mā te 'nyat puruṣavyāghra dānād bhavatu darśanam ayaśasyam ato 'nyat syād adharmyaṃ ca mahābhuja
english: Let your view, O tiger among men, be of nothing but giving; anything other than this would be inglorious and unrighteous, O mighty-armed one.

sanskrit: rājānam upatiṣṭhasva jyeṣṭhaṃ bhrātaram īśvaram arhas tvam asi dātuṃ vai nādātuṃ bharatarṣabha evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ kaunteyaṃ dharmarājo 'bhyapūjayat
english: Attend upon the king, your eldest brother and lord; it is for you to give, not to withhold, O bull of the Bharatas." As the son of Kuntī spoke thus, the King of Righteousness honored him.

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tu sakrodhaḥ provācedaṃ vacas tadā vayaṃ bhīṣmasya kurmeha pretakāryāṇi phalguna
english: But Bhīmasena, full of wrath, then spoke these words: "It is we who should perform the funeral rites for Bhīṣma here, O Phalguna,

sanskrit: somadattasya nṛpater bhūriśravasa eva ca bāhlīkasya ca rājarṣer droṇasya ca mahātmanaḥ
english: for King Somadatta, and for Bhūriśravas, and for the royal sage Bāhlīka, and for the great-souled Droṇa,

sanskrit: anyeṣāṃ caiva suhṛdāṃ kuntī karṇāya dāsyati śrāddhāni puruṣavyāghra mādāt kauravako nṛpaḥ
english: and for the other kinsmen; and Kuntī shall make the śrāddha offerings for Karṇa, O tiger among men—let not the Kaurava king bestow them.

sanskrit: iti me vartate buddhir mā vo nandantu śatravaḥ kaṣṭāt kaṣṭataraṃ yāntu sarve duryodhanādayaḥ yair iyaṃ pṛthivī sarvā ghātitā kulapāṃsanaiḥ
english: Such is my mind. Let not our enemies rejoice; let Duryodhana and all the rest go from misery to misery still greater—those defilers of their line by whom this whole earth was brought to slaughter.

sanskrit: kutas tvam adya vismṛtya vairaṃ dvādaśavārṣikam ajñātavāsagamanaṃ draupadīśokavardhanam kva tadā dhṛtarāṣṭrasya sneho 'smāsv abhavat tadā
english: How can you today forget the enmity of those twelve years, the going into hidden exile that swelled Draupadī's grief? Where then was Dhṛtarāṣṭra's affection for us in that hour?

sanskrit: kṛṣṇājinopasaṃvīto hṛtābharaṇabhūṣaṇaḥ sārdhaṃ pāñcālaputryā tvaṃ rājānam upajagmivān kva tadā droṇabhīṣmau tau somadatto 'pi vābhavat
english: Clad in a black antelope's hide, stripped of your ornaments and finery, you went before the king together with the daughter of Pāñcāla. Where then were those two, Droṇa and Bhīṣma, or Somadatta?

sanskrit: yatra trayodaśa samā vane vanyena jīvasi na tadā tvā pitā jyeṣṭhaḥ pitṛtvenābhivīkṣate
english: During the thirteen years in which you lived in the forest on its wild produce, the elder who is our father did not then regard you with a father's eyes.

sanskrit: kiṃ te tad vismṛtaṃ pārtha yad eṣa kulapāṃsanaḥ durvṛtto viduraṃ prāha dyūte kiṃ jitam ity uta
english: Have you forgotten, O Pārtha, how this defiler of the line, that wicked one, said to Vidura at the dicing, 'What has been won?'

sanskrit: tam evaṃvādinaṃ rājā kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ uvāca bhrātaraṃ dhīmāñ joṣam āsveti bhartsayan
english: To his brother speaking thus, King Yudhiṣṭhira, the wise son of Kuntī, said in rebuke, "Hold your peace and be still."

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca bhīma jyeṣṭho gurur me tvaṃ nāto 'nyad vaktum utsahe dhṛtarāṣṭro hi rājarṣiḥ sarvathā mānam arhati
english: Arjuna said: Bhīma, you are my elder and my teacher; beyond this I dare not speak. But Dhṛtarāṣṭra, that royal sage, deserves honor in every way.

sanskrit: na smaranty aparāddhāni smaranti sukṛtāni ca asaṃbhinnārthamaryādāḥ sādhavaḥ puruṣottamāḥ
english: The good, those best of men who never breach the bounds of duty, do not remember wrongs done to them, but remember the kindnesses.

sanskrit: idaṃ madvacanāt kṣattaḥ kauravaṃ brūhi pārthivam yāvad icchati putrāṇāṃ dātuṃ tāvad dadāmy aham
english: Say this from me, O Kṣattṛ, to the Kaurava king: 'However much you wish to give on behalf of your sons, so much do I give.'

sanskrit: bhīṣmādīnāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ suhṛdām upakāriṇām mama kośād iti vibho mā bhūd bhīmaḥ sudurmanāḥ
english: 'For Bhīṣma and all the rest, those friends who did us good service, let it be from my treasury,' O lord—and let Bhīma not be sore at heart.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity ukte dharmarājas tam arjunaṃ pratyapūjayat bhīmasenaḥ kaṭākṣeṇa vīkṣāṃ cakre dhanaṃjayam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When this had been spoken, the King of Righteousness honored Arjuna in return, while Bhīmasena cast a sidelong glance at Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa viduraṃ dhīmān vākyam āha yudhiṣṭhiraḥ na bhīmasene kopaṃ sa nṛpatiḥ kartum arhati
english: Then the wise Yudhiṣṭhira spoke these words to Vidura: "That king ought not to feel anger toward Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: parikliṣṭo hi bhīmo 'yaṃ himavṛṣṭyātapādibhiḥ duḥkhair bahuvidhair dhīmān araṇye viditaṃ tava
english: For this Bhīma was sorely afflicted by snow, rain, sun, and the like—by manifold sufferings in the forest, as you well know.

sanskrit: kiṃ tu madvacanād brūhi rājānaṃ bharatarṣabham yad yad icchasi yāvac ca gṛhyatāṃ madgṛhād iti
english: But say this from me to the king, that bull of the Bharatas: 'Whatever you wish, and however much, let it be taken from my house.'

sanskrit: yan mātsaryam ayaṃ bhīmaḥ karoti bhṛśaduḥkhitaḥ na tan manasi kartavyam iti vācyaḥ sa pārthivaḥ
english: 'The grudge that this Bhīma harbors, being grievously pained, ought not to be taken to heart'—so the king is to be told.

sanskrit: yan mamāsti dhanaṃ kiṃ cid arjunasya ca veśmani tasya svāmī mahārāja iti vācyaḥ sa pārthivaḥ
english: 'Whatever wealth there is of mine and in Arjuna's house, of that the great king is the master'—so the king is to be told.

sanskrit: dadātu rājā viprebhyo yatheṣṭaṃ kriyatāṃ vyayaḥ putrāṇāṃ suhṛdāṃ caiva gacchatv ānṛṇyam adya saḥ
english: Let the king give to the brahmins as he pleases; let the expenditure be made for his sons and his friends; let him this day pass free of his debt to them.

sanskrit: idaṃ cāpi śarīraṃ me tavāyattaṃ janādhipa dhanāni ceti viddhi tvaṃ kṣattar nāsty atra saṃśayaḥ
english: 'This body of mine too is at your disposal, O ruler of men, and so is my wealth'—know this, O Kṣattṛ; herein is no doubt.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktas tu rājñā sa viduro buddhisattamaḥ dhṛtarāṣṭram upetyedaṃ vākyam āha mahārthavat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by the king, Vidura, best of the wise, approached Dhṛtarāṣṭra and spoke these words full of weighty meaning:

sanskrit: ukto yudhiṣṭhiro rājā bhavadvacanam āditaḥ sa ca saṃśrutya vākyaṃ te praśaśaṃsa mahādyutiḥ
english: "King Yudhiṣṭhira was told your message from the first, and that one of great lustre, having heard your words, praised them.

sanskrit: bībhatsuś ca mahātejā nivedayati te gṛhān vasu tasya gṛhe yac ca prāṇān api ca kevalān
english: And Bībhatsu of great lustre offers you his houses, the wealth that is in his house, and even his very life.

sanskrit: dharmarājaś ca putras te rājyaṃ prāṇān dhanāni ca anujānāti rājarṣe yac cānyad api kiṃ cana
english: And the King of Righteousness, your son, grants you the kingdom, his life, his wealth, O royal sage, and whatever else there may be.

sanskrit: bhīmas tu sarvaduḥkhāni saṃsmṛtya bahulāny uta kṛcchrād iva mahābāhur anumanye viniḥśvasan
english: But Bhīma, the mighty-armed, recalling his many and manifold sorrows, gave his assent as if with difficulty, sighing deeply.

sanskrit: sa rājñā dharmaśīlena bhrātrā bībhatsunā tathā anunīto mahābāhuḥ sauhṛde sthāpito 'pi ca
english: He, the mighty-armed, was won over by his righteous brother the king and by Bībhatsu, and was set firm in friendship.

sanskrit: na ca manyus tvayā kārya iti tvāṃ prāha dharmarāṭ saṃsmṛtya bhīmas tad vairaṃ yad anyāyavad ācaret
english: And the King of Righteousness says to you: 'You ought to feel no anger if Bhīma, remembering that enmity, should act unjustly.'

sanskrit: evaṃprāyo hi dharmo 'yaṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ narādhipa yuddhe kṣatriyadharme ca nirato 'yaṃ vṛkodaraḥ
english: For such is by and large the duty of the kṣatriyas, O ruler of men; and this Vṛkodara is devoted to war and to the kṣatriya's code.

sanskrit: vṛkodarakṛte cāham arjunaś ca punaḥ punaḥ prasādayāva nṛpate bhavān prabhur ihāsti yat
english: For Vṛkodara's sake, both I and Arjuna again and again entreat you, O king; in this matter you are the lord.

sanskrit: pradadātu bhavān vittaṃ yāvad icchasi pārthiva tvam īśvaro no rājyasya prāṇānāṃ ceti bhārata
english: Let your honor bestow as much wealth as you wish, O king; you are the master of our kingdom and of our lives, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: brahmadeyāgrahārāṃś ca putrāṇāṃ caurdhvadehikam ito ratnāni gāś caiva dāsīdāsam ajāvikam
english: Grants of land to brahmins, and the funeral offerings for your sons, and from here jewels and cattle, maidservants and menservants, goats and sheep—

sanskrit: ānayitvā kuruśreṣṭho brāhmaṇebhyaḥ prayacchatu dīnāndhakṛpaṇebhyaś ca tatra tatra nṛpājñayā
english: let the best of the Kurus have these brought and bestow them upon the brahmins, and upon the wretched, the blind, and the destitute, here and there at the king's command.

sanskrit: bahvannarasapānāḍhyāḥ sabhā vidura kāraya gavāṃ nipānāny anyac ca vividhaṃ puṇyakarma yat
english: 'Cause halls richly furnished with abundant food, savory dishes, and drink to be built, Vidura, and watering-troughs for cattle, and whatever other various works of merit there are.'

sanskrit: iti mām abravīd rājā pārthaś caiva dhanaṃjayaḥ yad atrānantaraṃ kāryaṃ tad bhavān vaktum arhati
english: Thus the king spoke to me, and Pārtha Dhanaṃjaya likewise. Whatever next is to be done in this, it is for you to declare."

sanskrit: ity ukto vidureṇātha dhṛtarāṣṭro 'bhinandya tat manaś cakre mahādāne kārttikyāṃ janamejaya
english: Thus addressed by Vidura, Dhṛtarāṣṭra rejoiced at it and set his mind upon a great gift-giving on the full-moon of Kārttika, O Janamejaya.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca vidureṇaivam uktas tu dhṛtarāṣṭro janādhipaḥ prītimān abhavad rājā rājño jiṣṇoś ca karmaṇā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by Vidura, the king Dhṛtarāṣṭra, that ruler of men, was made glad by the conduct of the king Yudhiṣṭhira and of Jiṣṇu.

sanskrit: tato 'bhirūpān bhīṣmāya brāhmaṇān ṛṣisattamān putrārthe suhṛdāṃ caiva sa samīkṣya sahasraśaḥ
english: Then, on behalf of Bhīṣma, for his sons, and for his friends, he selected by the thousand suitable brahmins, those best of sages.

sanskrit: kārayitvānnapānāni yānāny ācchādanāni ca suvarṇamaṇiratnāni dāsīdāsaparicchadān
english: Having had prepared food and drink, conveyances and garments, gold, gems, and jewels, maidservants, menservants, and furnishings,

sanskrit: kambalājinaratnāni grāmān kṣetrān ajāvikam alaṃkārān gajān aśvān kanyāś caiva varastriyaḥ ādiśyādiśya viprebhyo dadau sa nṛpasattamaḥ
english: woolen blankets, hides and jewels, villages and fields, goats and sheep, ornaments, elephants and horses, and maidens, the choicest of women—pointing out each in turn, that best of kings gave them to the brahmins.

sanskrit: droṇaṃ saṃkīrtya bhīṣmaṃ ca somadattaṃ ca bāhlikam duryodhanaṃ ca rājānaṃ putrāṃś caiva pṛthak pṛthak jayadrathapurogāṃś ca suhṛdaś caiva sarvaśaḥ
english: Naming Droṇa and Bhīṣma, Somadatta and Bāhlika, and King Duryodhana, and his sons each one by one, and those headed by Jayadratha, and all his friends without exception,

sanskrit: sa śrāddhayajño vavṛdhe bahugodhanadakṣiṇaḥ anekadhanaratnaugho yudhiṣṭhiramate tadā
english: that śrāddha-sacrifice grew great, rich in fees of cattle and wealth, a flood of manifold riches and jewels, then carried out at Yudhiṣṭhira's pleasure.

sanskrit: aniśaṃ yatra puruṣā gaṇakā lekhakās tathā yudhiṣṭhirasya vacanāt tad āpṛcchanti taṃ nṛpam
english: There, ceaselessly, the men, the accountants, and the scribes, at the word of Yudhiṣṭhira, kept asking that king,

sanskrit: ājñāpaya kim etebhyaḥ pradeyaṃ dīyatām iti tad upasthitam evātra vacanānte pradṛśyate
english: "Command us: what is to be given to these? Let it be given"—and the very thing was shown ready to hand at the end of the speech.

sanskrit: śate deye daśaśataṃ sahasre cāyutaṃ tathā dīyate vacanād rājñaḥ kuntīputrasya dhīmataḥ
english: Where a hundred was to be given, a thousand was given, and where a thousand, then ten thousand, at the word of the wise king, the son of Kuntī.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa vasudhārābhir varṣamāṇo nṛpāmbudaḥ tarpayām āsa viprāṃs tān varṣan bhūmim ivāmbudaḥ
english: Thus that king, a rain-cloud raining showers of wealth, satisfied those brahmins, even as a cloud pouring rain upon the earth.

sanskrit: tato 'nantaram evātra sarvavarṇān mahīpatiḥ annapānarasaughena plāvayām āsa pārthivaḥ
english: Then immediately thereafter the lord of the earth, that king, flooded men of all the castes with a deluge of food, drink, and savory dishes.

sanskrit: savastraphenaratnaugho mṛdaṅganinadasvanaḥ gavāśvamakarāvarto nārīratnamahākaraḥ
english: With its foam of garments and its flood of jewels, its roar the sound of drums, its whirlpools the cattle and horses for sea-monsters, and women, those jewels, for its great mass of waters—
